title: Enforce branch-aware work-item completion and SemVer delivery
objective: Extend sdlc work-item validate, add sdlc work-item start --work-item <id>, and extend the installed Git hooks to support planning on the merge target, task processing on a started context branch, merge completion, primary-branch-only SemVer tagging, and remote push readiness, while introducing conditional work-item/v3 versionSuggestion metadata without adding a version suggest-new command.

branch.name: WI-0024-branch-aware-work-item-delivery-current
branch.rationale: The WI-0024 implementation is being processed on the current dedicated context branch created from the latest main baseline.

request.text:
Prepare a new .docs/work-items/* to update sdlc work-item validate to include branch validation. We want to ensure that the mergeTarget branch is the repository's master (or main), The mergeTarget must be a branch available on the remote (assuming there is a remote). If there's no remote, we can ensure that the branch exists in the local repository. Additionally, we'll ensure that the context.branch.name follows the format <work-item-id>-<slug>. We're allowed to commit new work items and work item updates on either the mergeTarget branch or the context.branch.name branch, but no other branches. Any work item specific processing, such as task processing MUST be committed to context.branch.name. We need to extend our pre-commit hook to detect if the changes staged in the commit are due to work item task processing, and if so, require that we're committing to context.branch.name. An error respones sufficient for the coding agent to take remedial action is required.

We additionally require a mechanism to remind the agent to merge (and if merging to the primary/main/master branch; tag) upon work item completion.

The net goal of this .docs/work-items/* is to force work item changes to happen on a branch, then to force merge when the work item is completed, and finally to enforce a tag and push to remote (if remote exists) following the merge.

use a release/version tag that follows semantic versioning. if possible, we can add an sdlc version suggest-new that attempts to categorize the changes between the mergeTarget and context.branch.name. Another option is to update sdlc/work-item/v1 to add a version suggestion field indicating major/minor/revision. Semantic versioning requires breaking changes to be a major version, minor changes are backwards compatible changes, and revisions are generally bugfixes/etc that don't impact any publicly facing APIs.

Create work-item/v3 with the new version-suggestion field and keep v2 historical records valid (recommended)

it's important that we don't tag non-primary branches.

remove the sdlc version suggest-new --work-item <id> -- this is superceded by the versionSuggestion information in sdlc/work-item

Prepare the new .docs/work-items/* and commit  the work item.

scope.name: branch-aware-validation
scope.description: Extend sdlc work-item validate with merge-target availability, primary-branch, context-branch naming, current-branch, detached-HEAD, and remote/local fallback checks.
scope.reason: Work-item records must be processed and delivered only within their declared branch context.

scope.name: task-processing-branch-gate
scope.description: Detect staged task-processing changes under .docs/work-items/<id>/steps/**/*.{yaml,yml,json} and require commits containing processing changes to run on exactly context.branch.name, while allowing complete initial work-item/task planning materialization and ordinary work-item record updates on either allowed branch.
scope.reason: Planning may be completed on the merge target, but task processing is work-item-specific state and must not be committed directly to the merge target or an unrelated branch.

scope.name: work-item-v3-version-suggestion
scope.description: Define a work-item/v3 schema that adds versionSuggestion impact, rationale, and disclaimer metadata while preserving work-item/v2 for historical records.
scope.reason: Semantic-version impact belongs with the work-item's authoritative planning information and must be durable without persisting current or suggested version numbers.

scope.name: primary-branch-only-release
scope.description: Require SemVer release tags only on the primary mergeTarget branch after merge; never create, validate, or push release tags for context branches or other non-primary branches.
scope.reason: Tags identify delivered primary-branch releases and must not be confused with in-progress task branches.

scope.name: merge-tag-push-completion
scope.description: Add pre-commit, post-merge, and pre-push enforcement/reminders for merge completion, deterministic SemVer calculation from the latest annotated tag and aggregate versionSuggestion impact, primary-branch tag alignment, and remote push readiness.
scope.reason: The net delivery goal is branch processing, merge, primary-branch-only tagging, and remote publication when a remote exists.

scope.name: remediation-and-legacy-policy
scope.description: Return complete actionable branch/version/tag/push findings and define explicit compatibility remediation for historical v2 records that predate the new branch policy.
scope.reason: Agents need enough context to fix branch or delivery violations without guessing, and existing records must not be silently reinterpreted.

scope.name: work-item-start-lifecycle
scope.description: Add sdlc work-item start --work-item <id> to verify the merge-target branch, create and switch to context.branch.name, set context.branch.created=true, and commit that state transition on the new context branch.
scope.reason: A deterministic start boundary separates planning/task generation on the merge target from subsequent task processing on the work-item branch.

scope.name: task-format-and-schema-version-policy
scope.description: Support task records with .yaml, .yml, and .json extensions and select work-item validation behavior conditionally by the work-item schema URI, preserving v2 historical behavior while applying v3 versionSuggestion rules.
scope.reason: The repository must intentionally support all declared task file forms and evolve the work-item schema without silently changing v2 semantics.

scope.name: deterministic-release-baseline
scope.description: Use only annotated, SemVer-shaped tags reachable from the primary branch, select the highest numeric SemVer baseline, use 0.0.1 when no baseline exists, reject package versions ahead of the calculated version, and aggregate multiple completed work items by major > minor > revision.
scope.reason: Primary-branch delivery must be deterministic and must require human intervention for unexpected package-version state.

nonGoals.name: version-suggest-command
nonGoals.description: Do not add sdlc version suggest-new --work-item <id> or any replacement command that generates versionSuggestion outside the work-item record.
nonGoals.reason: The requested design supersedes the command with versionSuggestion information persisted in the work-item schema/record.

nonGoals.name: version-number-persistence
nonGoals.description: Do not add currentVersion or suggestedVersion fields to the work item; infer the deterministic release version at primary-branch push time from the latest annotated SemVer tag and aggregate impact.
nonGoals.reason: VersionSuggestion records impact, while repository/package state determines the actual release number.

nonGoals.name: non-primary-tagging
nonGoals.description: Do not create, require, or push release tags on context.branch.name or any non-primary branch.
nonGoals.reason: Only the merged main/master branch represents a released delivery boundary.

nonGoals.name: silent-v2-rewrite
nonGoals.description: Do not silently rewrite historical work-item/v2 records or reinterpret unavailable master/main branches as equivalent.
nonGoals.reason: Versioned schemas retain their meaning and legacy records require explicit remediation or migration evidence.

nonGoals.name: remote-when-absent
nonGoals.description: Do not require remote push operations when the repository has no configured remote; local merge and primary-branch tag checks still apply.
nonGoals.reason: Remote publication is conditional on repository configuration.

items.name: branch-context-validation
items.description: sdlc work-item validate must require mergeTarget.branch to be main or master, verify it on a remote when a remote exists or locally when no remote exists, require context.branch.name to match <work-item-id>-<lowercase-kebab-case-slug>, and allow the current branch only when it is the merge target or context branch.
items.reason: Branch context is the repository coordination boundary for every work item.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Valid local and remote branch matrices pass, including a main merge target on origin/main and a no-remote local fallback; invalid merge targets, missing branches, detached HEAD, malformed context names, and unrelated current branches return actionable findings.
The validation response identifies currentBranch, mergeTargetBranch, contextBranch, remoteAvailability, localAvailability, and exact remediation commands for every branch-policy failure.

items.name: task-processing-branch-enforcement
items.description: The work-item pre-commit validation must detect staged task-processing files under .docs/work-items/<id>/steps/ and require the current branch to equal that work item's context.branch.name; ordinary work-item.json creation/update commits may run on either allowed branch.
items.reason: Task processing must happen on the work-item branch while intake and merge-target record updates remain possible on the primary branch.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A staged task-processing change on context.branch.name passes, the same change on mergeTarget or another branch fails, and the failure prints the complete validation response before blocking the commit.
A staged work-item.json-only change passes on either allowed branch and does not incorrectly trigger task-processing branch enforcement.

items.name: version-suggestion-schema
items.description: The future work-item/v3 schema must add versionSuggestion metadata with impact major, minor, or revision, a non-empty rationale, and a disclaimer that the recommendation must be increased if final changes exceed expectations; versionSuggestion is required in every v3 lifecycle state, including planned, accepted, and active, and must not contain currentVersion or suggestedVersion.
items.reason: Version impact is authoritative planning information from the beginning of the work-item lifecycle, while actual release version calculation belongs to primary-branch delivery state.

acceptanceCriteria.description: work-item/v3 preserves the v2 contract and adds a closed versionSuggestion object whose impact, rationale, and disclaimer fields validate representative major, minor, and revision records.

Every v3 record in planned, accepted, active, implemented, and complete states requires versionSuggestion; a missing object fails sdlc work-item validate and the pre-commit hook reports the complete response.
Historical work-item/v2 records remain valid, skip version-specific versionSuggestion checks, and no version-suggestion command is added or required.

items.name: deterministic-primary-release
items.description: After completed work items are merged onto main/master, pre-push validation must aggregate versionSuggestion impact using major > minor > revision, select only the highest numeric SemVer among annotated SemVer-shaped tags reachable from the primary branch, use 0.0.1 when no such baseline exists, derive the expected next SemVer, and require package.json.version plus an annotated tag with that exact version at the primary-branch tip.
items.reason: The release check must be deterministic even though impact classification is inferred in the work-item record.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Revision increments patch, minor increments minor and resets patch, and major increments major and resets minor/patch; when no annotated reachable SemVer baseline exists the expected first version is 0.0.1; package.json.version and the annotated tag must match the calculated version.
A package.json.version already ahead of the calculated version fails with an actionable human-intervention finding rather than being changed automatically.

When multiple completed work items are included in one primary-branch push, their impacts aggregate by selecting the highest impact and incrementing once; a context-branch or unrelated-branch push never creates, requires, or accepts a release tag.

items.name: merge-push-completion
items.description: Completion enforcement must remind after merge to merge the context branch, tag only the primary branch, and push the primary branch plus tag when a remote exists; no-remote repositories must report local completion without requiring push.
items.reason: The delivery lifecycle must end in a merged, correctly tagged primary branch and conditional remote publication.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Post-merge output identifies completed work items, required merge/tag/push actions, expected version, tag target, and remote state with actionable commands.

Pre-push rejects a primary-branch update with a missing/mismatched/unannotated/non-tip tag or missing remote tag, and accepts a consistent branch/tag push; no-remote fallback accepts consistent local state.

items.name: legacy-and-test-gates
items.description: The implementation must define explicit remediation for historical v2 records, preserve full validation responses, support .yaml/.yml/.json task records, and pass complete branch/remote/tag/push integration tests, schema audit, and work-item validation before commit.
items.reason: Existing records predate the policy and every enforcement layer needs deterministic regression evidence.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Historical records with unavailable merge targets or legacy branch names produce explicit migration/remediation findings rather than silent branch reinterpretation; v2 records continue branch/merge/push checks while skipping versionSuggestion checks.
The complete typecheck, build, test, schema-audit, and sdlc work-item validate gates pass before the WI-0024 work-item commit.

items.name: work-item-start-command
items.description: sdlc work-item start --work-item <id> must verify the current branch is mergeTarget.branch, create and switch to context.branch.name, set context.branch.created=true, and commit the state transition on the new context branch; it must be safe and idempotent when already started.
items.reason: Starting processing must be an explicit branch transition after planning is complete on the merge target.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Starting from mergeTarget creates the declared context branch, switches to it, updates context.branch.created to true, and commits only that state transition on context.branch.name.

The command refuses unrelated current branches, detached HEAD, unavailable merge targets, pre-existing unexpected context branches, or unsafe unrelated staged changes with complete remediation findings, and repeated start on the created context branch is an idempotent no-op response.

items.name: planning-and-task-format
items.description: Complete initial work-item and task planning may be generated and committed on mergeTarget.branch; after start, processing changes are restricted to context.branch.name, and task discovery/validation supports .yaml, .yml, and .json task records with extension-appropriate parsing.
items.reason: The current model supports both complete upfront planning and incremental planning without forcing task generation to wait for branch creation, while task processing still requires isolation.

acceptanceCriteria.description: New task records that remain unprocessed/planned may be added on either allowed branch; changes to processingStatus, task.status, task.result, or existing task records require context.branch.name.
Equivalent valid task envelopes stored as .yaml, .yml, or .json are discovered, parsed, schema-validated, and included in work-item validation.

items.name: completion-condition-and-push-refs
items.description: Completion enforcement must define completion as work-item.status=complete plus all required task processing/results complete, and pre-push must separately inspect branch and tag ref updates to reject release-tag creation, replacement, or deletion outside the primary branch or without a matching primary-branch tip.
items.reason: The merge and release lifecycle needs an exact completion trigger and complete Git ref-update coverage.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A completed work item is eligible for merge/tag/push reminders only when its work-item status and required task terminal states satisfy the declared completion condition.

Pre-push accepts context-branch pushes without release tags, enforces release checks only for the primary branch, and rejects lightweight, non-tip, deleted, replaced, or context-branch SemVer release tags with actionable findings.

versionSuggestion.rationale: Adds branch-aware work-item validation, an explicit work-item start command, task-processing and primary-delivery hook enforcement, work-item v3 metadata, and agent process documentation without breaking existing work-item v2 records.
versionSuggestion.disclaimer: This is an inferred recommendation; increase the impact if final changes are larger or more breaking than expected.
